title: Strict transform commutes with flat étale base change under generic-point control
statement: Let $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ be the blowup of a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [def-nagata-global-blowup], let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $v:W\to X$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] (in particular, $v$ may be étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]). Assume that every irreducible component of $Z\times_XW$ has generic point mapping to the generic point of an irreducible component of $Z$ (equivalently, no component of the pullback lies over a proper closed subset of its corresponding component). Write $Z^{\mathrm{st}}\hookrightarrow X^+$ for the strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Then the canonical flat-base-change identification $X^+\times_XW\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_W}(W)$ [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map], with $\mathcal I\mathcal O_W$ the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal], identifies $Z^{\mathrm{st}}\times_XW$ with the strict transform of $Z\times_XW$ in $X^+\times_XW$; this equality is scheme-theoretic closure of the common inverse image of $Z\setminus V(\mathcal I)$.

source.place: Tag 081I, lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image (flat base change of the quasi-compact scheme-theoretic image defining the strict-transform closure)

proof.text: Put P = Bl_I(X), U = X \ V(I), q : P ×_X W → P and π_W : P ×_X W → W. The ideal-module bridge [lem-pqf-finite-type-ideal-module] converts I.ofFiniteType to finite type of I.toModules. The quasi-compactness clause of [lem-trf-finite-center-open-closure-kernel-data], applied to the relevant structure maps to X and to W, makes the preserved-open inclusions quasi-compact. The source-library ker_strictTransformMap then identifies the ideal of each strict transform with the kernel of its preserved-open map to its ambient blowup [def-nagata-strict-transform].

Construct p : (Z ×_X W) ×_W (P ×_X W) → Z ×_X P by its Z and P projections. Pasting the two defining fibre-product squares and cancelling the original square proves IsPullback p b a q, where a and b are the ambient projections. Restrict p to the inverse image of the preserved open and paste again. Since q is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], [lem-sfb-scheme-image-flat-base-change], in its proved ker_of_isPullback form, identifies the pulled-back kernel of the open map with the kernel of the base-changed open map. The equality q⁻¹(π⁻¹U) = π_W⁻¹(v⁻¹U) follows from the pullback equation. This is the second conjunct.

Let e : Bl_(I O_W)(W) ≅ P ×_X W be the specified flat blowup comparison [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map, thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change]. The map on the fibre products with Z ×_X W induced by e.hom is an isomorphism, and its square over e.hom is cartesian. The support-comap formula identifies (I.comap v).support.compl with v⁻¹U; the equation e.hom ≫ π_W = (I.comap v).blowupMap identifies the preserved opens. Apply the same open-kernel comparison [lem-sfb-scheme-image-flat-base-change] along the flat isomorphism e.hom, then pull back along e.inv. Functoriality of ideal pullback and e.inv ≫ e.hom = identity give the first conjunct. No generic-point argument is needed; its hypothesis stays verbatim.

proof_origin.place: Tag 081I, lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image, applied directly to the preserved-open maps; divisors.tex Tags 080D and 0805 for strict transform and the specified blowup comparison. Pullback pasting and open restriction are explicit Lean proofs by D9.
